messages.author: c3cde982f551021c
messages.subject: mesh.t
parts:
Hello everyone:

When running the following code:

knots <- seq(1, 108, length.out = 36)
mesh.t <- inla.mesh.1d(knots, degree = 2)

The inla.stack function doesn't report an error when I set degree=1, while it reports an error （because of the difference in the number of rows or cols）when I set degree=2. What could be the reason for this and how to fix it?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] mesh.t
parts:
Hi,
With degree=2 (or with some other boundary conditions) the number of basis functions does not equal the number of knots. I’m guessing you have some code that assumes the number of basis functions to be 36?
Make sure you have the latest release of the fmesher package, and use fm_dof(mesh.t) to obtain the correct number.
Finn

messages.author: c3cde982f551021c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] mesh.t
parts:
Thank you
I only set the knots number to be 36, did not set the number of basis functions.
You are right.
For degree=1, fm_dof(mesh.t) is 36（equal to knots number)
For degree=2, fm_dof(mesh.t) is 35  (not equal to knots number), so leading to an error.
Now I set the boundary condition to be c("neumann","free"), and degree=2,   fm_dof(mesh.t) is 36 again, and the code is running successfully. 
But I'm not quite sure what's behind it and I'm not quite sure if it makes sense to change it.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] mesh.t
parts:
The number of basis of functions should not equal the number of knots in general. It’s just that most example use degree=1 and Neumann boundaries, and therefore get away with not implementing the it in the correct way. If you always use fm_dof() for the number of latent variables in the model, and always use fm_basis() or inla.spde.make.A() to compute the “A-matrix” link in observation locations/times to the model, then you shouldn’t get an error, so presumably some part of your code takes a shortcut that isn’t generally valid.
Finn
